title: Justifying Each Step
_notes: Source of truth for the 1.3 practice set. Every step of an equation is named by the property that justifies it, and the build reads that property from the two equations (tools/build_exercises.py: step_kind), so a step can never be given the wrong name. "match" and "multi" use check "step" / "step:<Property>" (left or option = "A → B", the property is Addition, Subtraction, Multiplication, Division, Distributive or Combine) and "valid-from:<equation>" (option = an equation with the same solution). Typed answers (kind "num") carry "derive": operand:<Property> (the number a step adds, subtracts, multiplies by or divides by; q = "A → B"), solve (the solution of the equation q) or first-error (q = a student's work, one line per row; the answer is the number of the first line that stops having the first line's solution). Every wrong value names its mistake "m" (operand: sign, result, start; solve: sign-k, sign-x, no-divide, ignore-k, order; first-error: last, before, after, first) and the build recomputes it. "a_read" / "a_show" say and show an answer that is not just the number. Chips: ADD blue, SUBTRACT purple, MULTIPLY yellow, DIVIDE green, DIST yellow, COMBINE green; for a student's work OK green, ERROR red, CARRY ink. See docs/exercises.md.

exercises.prompt: Match each step with the property that justifies it.
exercises.read: Match each step with the property that justifies it.
exercises.say_answer: Every step has its property: each one undoes its opposite operation.

pairs.why: Five was added to x, so you undo it by subtracting five from both sides.
pairs.say: X plus five equals nine became x equals four. Five was subtracted from both sides: the subtraction property.

pairs.why: Three was subtracted from x, so you undo it by adding three to both sides.
pairs.say: X minus three equals seven became x equals ten. Three was added to both sides: the addition property.

pairs.why: x was divided by two, so you undo it by multiplying both sides by two.
pairs.say: X over two equals six became x equals twelve. Both sides were multiplied by two: the multiplication property.

pairs.why: x was multiplied by three, so you undo it by dividing both sides by three.
pairs.say: Three x equals twelve became x equals four. Both sides were divided by three: the division property.

exercises.prompt: What number was subtracted from both sides? Type it.
exercises.read: In this step, x plus eight equals fifteen becomes x equals seven. What number was subtracted from both sides?
say: Eight was added to x, so the subtraction property takes eight away from both sides. Eight minus eight is zero, and fifteen minus eight is seven.

wrong.why: The step subtracts eight, but the number itself is eight, not negative eight.
wrong.say: write the subtraction as a negative number

wrong.why: Seven is the new right side. The number taken away is eight.
wrong.say: copy the result of the step

wrong.why: Fifteen is the old right side. Eight is the number taken away.
wrong.say: copy the number on the other side

exercises.prompt: Select all the moves that are allowed on both sides of an equation.
exercises.read: Select all the moves that are allowed on both sides of an equation.
exercises.say_answer: Adding, subtracting, and multiplying both sides by the same number are allowed. Changing only one side, or dividing by zero, is not.

options.t: Add the same number to both sides
options.why: Adding the same amount to both sides keeps the balance.
options.say: Add the same number to both sides. Yes: the two sides stay equal.

options.t: Subtract the same number from both sides
options.why: Taking the same amount from both sides keeps the balance.
options.say: Subtract the same number from both sides. Yes: the two sides stay equal.

options.t: Add a number to one side only
options.why: Changing only one side breaks the balance.
options.say: Add a number to one side only. No: the balance tips, so the sides are no longer equal.

options.why: Division by zero has no answer.
options.say: Divide both sides by zero. No: division by zero has no answer.

options.t: Multiply both sides by the same number
options.why: Multiplying both sides by the same number keeps the balance.
options.say: Multiply both sides by the same number. Yes: the two sides stay equal.

exercises.prompt: Which of these steps use the addition property of equality? Select all that apply.
exercises.read: Which of these steps use the addition property of equality? Choose all that apply.
exercises.say_answer: Three steps use the addition property. Each one adds the same number to both sides to undo a subtraction.

options.why: Four is added to both sides to undo the minus four.
options.say: X minus four equals nine becomes x equals thirteen. Four is added to both sides, so this is the addition property.

options.why: Four is taken away from both sides: that is the subtraction property.
options.say: X plus four equals nine becomes x equals five. Four is subtracted from both sides, so this is the subtraction property, not addition.

options.why: Seven is added to both sides to undo the minus seven.
options.say: X minus seven equals two becomes x equals nine. Seven is added to both sides: the addition property.

options.why: Both sides are divided by three: the division property.
options.say: Three x equals twelve becomes x equals four. Both sides are divided by three, so this is the division property.

options.why: One is added to both sides to undo the minus one.
options.say: X minus one equals six becomes x equals seven. One is added to both sides: the addition property.

exercises.prompt: Match each step with its reason.
exercises.read: Match each step with its reason.
exercises.say_answer: Every step has its reason. Opening the parentheses is the distributive property, collecting like terms is combining like terms, and each move on both sides is a property of equality.

pairs.why: The parentheses are gone: two was multiplied into x and into three.
pairs.say: Two times the quantity x plus three became two x plus six. The parentheses are gone, so this is the distributive property.

pairs.why: Three x and two x are like terms, so their coefficients are added.
pairs.say: Three x plus two x became five x. Like terms were collected, so this is combining like terms.

pairs.why: Both sides were divided by four.
pairs.say: Four x equals twenty became x equals five. Both sides were divided by four: the division property.

pairs.why: Both sides were multiplied by three.
pairs.say: X over three equals four became x equals twelve. Both sides were multiplied by three: the multiplication property.

pairs.why: Six was added to both sides.
pairs.say: X minus six equals one became x equals seven. Six was added to both sides: the addition property.

exercises.prompt: What number were both sides multiplied by? Type it.
exercises.read: In this step, x over four equals three becomes x equals twelve. What number were both sides multiplied by?
say: X was divided by four, so the multiplication property multiplies both sides by four. X over four times four is x, and three times four is twelve.

wrong.why: The step multiplies by four, not by negative four.
wrong.say: give the number a minus sign

wrong.why: Twelve is the new right side. The number you multiply by is four.
wrong.say: copy the result of the step

wrong.why: Three is the old right side. The number you multiply by is four.
wrong.say: copy the number on the other side

exercises.prompt: Starting from 3x + 2 = 11, which of these could be the next line? Select all that apply.
exercises.read: Starting from three x plus two equals eleven, which of these could be the next line? Choose all that apply.
exercises.say_answer: Two lines follow: three x equals nine, and six x plus four equals twenty-two. Each one does the same thing to both sides.

options.why: Two was subtracted from both sides.
options.say: Three x equals nine. Two was subtracted from both sides, so this line follows.

options.why: Both sides were multiplied by two.
options.say: Six x plus four equals twenty-two. Both sides were multiplied by two, so this line follows.

options.why: Two was added to the right side instead of being subtracted.
options.say: Three x equals thirteen. Two was added to the right side instead of subtracted, so this line does not follow.

options.why: Only the three x was divided by three. Everything on both sides must be divided.
options.say: X plus two equals eleven over three. Only the three x was divided by three, so this line does not follow.

options.why: Two was subtracted from the right side only.
options.say: Three x plus two equals nine. Two was subtracted from one side only, so the sides are no longer equal.

exercises.prompt: What number were both sides divided by? Type it, with its sign.
exercises.read: In this step, negative five x equals thirty becomes x equals negative six. What number were both sides divided by?
say: X is multiplied by negative five, so the division property divides both sides by negative five. Negative five x over negative five is x, and thirty over negative five is negative six.

wrong.why: Dividing both sides by five leaves negative x. To get x alone, divide by negative five.
wrong.say: ignore the minus sign

wrong.why: Negative six is the answer for x, not the number you divide by.
wrong.say: copy the new right side

wrong.why: Thirty is the old right side. The number you divide by is the coefficient, negative five.
wrong.say: copy the number on the other side

exercises.prompt: Solve for x. Type its value.
exercises.read: Solve three times the quantity x minus two equals twelve. Type the value of x.
say: Distribute the three: three times x is three x, and three times two is six. The distributive property gives three x minus six.
Add six to both sides, by the addition property of equality. Three x equals eighteen.
Divide both sides by three, by the division property of equality. X equals six.

wrong.why: Three x minus six: you undo the minus six by adding six, not by subtracting it.
wrong.say: subtract six instead of adding it

wrong.why: Three x equals eighteen is not finished. Divide both sides by three.
wrong.say: stop before the last division

wrong.why: Dividing by three gives x minus two equals four. The minus two still has to be undone.
wrong.say: forget to undo the minus two

exercises.prompt: Which line of the student's work is the first one that is wrong? Type its number: the first line is line 1.
exercises.read: A student's work is on the screen, line one at the top. Which line is the first one that is wrong?
say: The first step subtracts x from both sides. That is the subtraction property, so line two is fine.
The next step should add three to both sides, by the addition property. The student subtracted three instead, so line three is wrong.
The last step divides both sides by three. That step is fine on its own, but it carries the error, so line four is wrong too.

wrong.why: Line four is only where the wrong answer shows up. The mistake happened earlier.
wrong.say: point at the final answer

wrong.why: Line two is fine: subtracting x from both sides is allowed.
wrong.say: blame the line before the mistake

wrong.why: Line one is the equation the student was given.
wrong.say: blame the given equation

exercises.prompt: Which of these steps use the subtraction property of equality? Select all that apply.
exercises.read: Which of these steps use the subtraction property of equality? Choose all that apply.
exercises.say_answer: Three steps use the subtraction property: taking nine away, taking three x away, and taking six away. In each one, the same amount leaves both sides.

options.why: Nine is taken away from both sides.
options.say: X plus nine equals twelve becomes x equals three. Nine is subtracted from both sides: the subtraction property.

options.why: Three x is taken away from both sides. The amount can contain x.
options.say: Five x equals three x plus eight becomes two x equals eight. Three x is subtracted from both sides: the subtraction property.

options.why: Two is added to both sides: that is the addition property.
options.say: X minus two equals seven becomes x equals nine. Two is added to both sides, so this is the addition property.

options.why: Both sides are divided by four: the division property.
options.say: Four x equals twenty becomes x equals five. Both sides are divided by four, so this is the division property.

options.why: Six is taken away from both sides.
options.say: Three x plus six equals twenty-one becomes three x equals fifteen. Six is subtracted from both sides: the subtraction property.

exercises.prompt: Solve for x. Type its value.
exercises.read: Solve five x plus seven equals three x plus nineteen. Type the value of x.
say: Subtract three x from both sides, by the subtraction property of equality. That leaves two x plus seven equals nineteen.
Subtract seven from both sides, by the subtraction property of equality. Two x equals twelve.
Divide both sides by two, by the division property of equality. X equals six.

wrong.why: You undo the plus seven by subtracting seven, not by adding it. Adding gives two x equals twenty-six.
wrong.say: add seven instead of subtracting it

wrong.why: Two x equals twelve is not finished. Divide both sides by two.
wrong.say: stop before the last division

wrong.why: Nineteen minus seven is positive twelve. Seven minus nineteen flips the sign.
wrong.say: subtract in the wrong order

exercises.prompt: Which line of the student's work is the first one that is wrong? Type its number: the first line is line 1.
exercises.read: A student's work is on the screen, line one at the top. Which line is the first one that is wrong?
say: The first step distributes the four, by the distributive property, so line two is fine.
The second step subtracts two x from both sides, by the subtraction property, so line three is fine.
The third step should add four to both sides, by the addition property. The student subtracted four instead, so line four is wrong.
The last step divides by two, which is allowed, but it carries the error.

wrong.why: Line five is only where the wrong answer shows up. The mistake happened earlier.
wrong.say: point at the final answer

wrong.why: Line three is fine: subtracting two x from both sides is allowed.
wrong.say: blame the line before the mistake

wrong.why: Line one is the equation the student was given.
wrong.say: blame the given equation

exercises.prompt: These are the four steps of one solution. Match each step with its reason.
exercises.read: These are the four steps of one solution. Match each step with its reason.
exercises.say_answer: Opening the parentheses is the distributive property. Collecting three x and two x is combining like terms. Adding three to both sides is the addition property, and dividing by five is the division property.

pairs.why: The parentheses are gone: three was multiplied into x and into negative one.
pairs.say: Three times the quantity x minus one became three x minus three. The parentheses are gone: the distributive property.

pairs.why: Three x and two x are like terms, so they become five x.
pairs.say: Three x plus two x became five x. Like terms were collected: combining like terms.

pairs.why: Three was added to both sides to undo the minus three.
pairs.say: Three was added to both sides to undo the minus three: the addition property.

pairs.why: Both sides were divided by five.
pairs.say: Both sides were divided by five: the division property.
